answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can claim work, with rewards released only after independent peers verify completed tasks. The island of identities is then costly to multiply: a sybil operator must fund every account and risks losing its stake when it submits fabricated results. A mesa of trusted reviewers can check samples, while a meadow of low-value tasks lets newcomers build reputation gradually rather than buying instant influence.
